short_description: Consumer-facing physical trait that reports a cautious panel-relative signal related to lean body mass tendency within the current local reference panel.
summary_note: Usable consumer-facing physical trait with workable raw-array support and a clearer interpretation boundary between inherited lean-mass tendency and current measured body composition, muscle size, or training status for the no-imputation workflow.
what_it_measures: A panel-relative polygenic signal associated with lean body mass tendency, based on a score reported as whole body fat free mass and calibrated within the current local empirical reference panel.
interpretation_template: Lean body mass tendency is presented here as a cautious panel-relative body-composition signal, not as a direct measurement of your current muscle mass, fat-free mass, or fitness level. {interpretation}
caution_text: Use as a cautious panel-relative signal only. No imputation or ancestry-adjusted normalization is used, and the output should not be treated as a deterministic real-world result, a direct body-composition measurement, or fitness advice.
limitations: Percentiles and z-scores are relative to the local reference panel, not to a population-wide benchmark.

Real-world lean body mass depends strongly on sex, age, hormones, training, diet, illness, medication use, and hydration status, so this should not be treated as a precise estimate of current body composition.
The underlying reported trait is whole body fat free mass, which is broader than visible muscle alone and can include bone, organs, and body water.
confidence_note: Confidence reflects overlap and reference robustness under the no-imputation raw-array workflow, not certainty about the real-world trait.
reference_note: Percentiles and z-scores are calibrated against a local empirical reference artifact built from raw-array files in this project; they are panel-relative, not population-wide.
